bench_setup = function() {
	set.seed(20261117)
	n = 8L
	X = cbind(x1 = rnorm(n), x2 = rnorm(n))
	D = EDI:::optimal_blocks_distance_matrix_cpp(X, dist_code = 3L)
	storage.mode(D) = "double"
	des = EDI::DesignFixedOptimalBlocks$new(B = 4L, method = "ompr", response_type = "continuous", n = n)
	list(D = D, priv = des$.__enclos_env__$private)
}
candidate:
bench_run = function(d) {
	n = nrow(d$D)
	D = d$D
	diag(D) = 0
	m = nbpMatching::nonbimatch(nbpMatching::distancematrix(D))$matches
	partner = integer(n)
	partner[m$Group1.Row] = as.integer(m$Group2.Row)
	as.integer(pmin(seq_len(n), partner))
}
notes: Times the exact block solve for n=8, B=4 (pairs) on the Mahalanobis distance matrix EDI builds: the real private ompr/GLPK MILP method (reached through the R6 private env, untimed construction in setup) vs nbpMatching::nonbimatch as helper_matching.R:44 calls it. Both return each unit's block as the smallest unit index in it, so labels are compared exactly. Risks: ROI.plugin.glpk needs the system GLPK library on the runner, and nonbimatch's integer scaling could pick a different near-tied optimum (unlikely with continuous random X); n is kept at 8 because the MILP is exponential.
